title: Is A World War Imminent?
summary: A former Green Beret argues, during the 2026 US-Israel war on Iran, that a true world war is very unlikely because neither Russia nor China will fight for Iran and the US military and economic lead is overwhelming.

assertions.quote: saying World War II is imminent or World War II is coming, how how likely is that? I think it's very unlikely.

verdicts.note: Metaculus's 3.3k forecasters put a 'World War Three' (a war involving 30% of world GDP or half the population, with 10 million dead) at 22% for the whole 2019-2050 window, far below even odds for the next few years.
Metaculus's 431 forecasters put a US-Russia war (1,000 battle deaths a year between them) at 8% for the whole period to 2050, far below likely within a few years.
In FRI's 2024 survey the median expert/superforecaster put 500+ militarized deaths between Russia and the US by 2030 at 5%/1.8%, and between China and the US at 10%/6%.

In the Atlantic Council's late-2025 survey of 447 strategists, just over 40% envisioned a multifront great-power world war within the next decade: a sizable minority, but under half even over ten years.
Eurasia Group's 2026 outlook says US-China conflict is not imminent and US-Russia tensions are not set to spiral out of control.

About 620 experts surveyed by CFR gave a severe Taiwan Strait crisis and Russia-NATO armed clashes an even chance in 2026; these could draw the US into conflict, but a crisis or clash is not a great-power war.
Clauset's stationary model puts a WWII-sized war at about 43% per century, a few percent over a few years: elevated over the long run but far below even odds in the near term.
Braumoeller estimates about a 13% chance per century of a war killing over 1% of the world's population, which is serious but not likely within a few years.

Metaculus's 'World War Three before 2050?' stands at 22% over about 24 years (3.3k forecasters), and the question conditional on AGI arriving puts World War III within five years of AGI at 4% (66 forecasters), both far under even odds for the next few years.

assertions.quote: Are the written treaties which compel Russia to go to war if Iran goes to war? Clearly not.
I don't think China actually has the ability to pull off a successful invasion of Taiwan.

verdicts.note: Wargames find an invasion very costly and often failing if the US intervenes, but the PLA's amphibious and strike capacity is growing and the outcome is uncertain.
A linked Metaculus forecast gives 65% that China controls Taiwan after an invasion, which contradicts a lack of capability to take it by force.

DoD finds the PLAN 'almost certainly' lacks the conventional lift for a large-scale amphibious assault and is not building more landing ships, though it trains with civilian roll-on/roll-off ships to fill the gap.

Against a US-backed defense, none of CSIS's 18 pessimistic runs produced a clear Chinese success, but 3 ended in stalemate trending toward China; the result depends on US intervention, so it does not show China lacks the capability against Taiwan alone.
DDIS (Dec 2025): 'It is highly unlikely that China currently possesses the capability to launch a successful invasion', though it expects readiness to grow.
US intelligence says the PLA is making steady but uneven progress toward the capability and that an invasion carries a high risk of failure, so the capability is incomplete but growing.

assertions.quote: this is the part where I accuse people of conducting what I like to call Excel spreadsheet warfare.

verdicts.note: Quality, training, logistics and integration decide outcomes, as the 1991 Gulf War and Russia's 2022 performance showed against raw counts.
CSIS: 'wars are not decided solely by aggregate or abstract capabilities'; geography (160 km from China, 8,000+ km from Hawaii) favours China despite US quality advantages.

assertions.quote: Like we we outspend China and Russia combined, right?

verdicts.note: SIPRI estimates US spending well above the sum of China's and Russia's at market exchange rates, though purchasing-power comparisons narrow the gap.
SIPRI puts 2025 US spending at $954 billion against an estimated $336 billion for China and $190 billion for Russia ($526 billion combined), at market exchange rates.

assertions.quote: you had a number of nations where economic and military parody existed.

verdicts.note: Power-transition research links great wars to narrowing power gaps, but wars have also begun between unequal sides and the US lead over China has narrowed.

assertions.quote: Russia's already lost hundreds of thousands of troops over the last four years in Ukraine. Can can they really take on all of NATO?
Russia which has a vastly superior air force to Ukraine and yet they cannot achieve air dominance or air superiority.

verdicts.note: Ukrainian ground-based air defence has kept Russian aircraft largely to stand-off weapons such as glide bombs throughout the war.

assertions.quote: exports have all but stopped due to the Iranians uh effectively closing the straight of Hormuz.
China doesn't see a benefit to losing US consumer markets
There is zero question that the Iranian military is not capable of standing up to the United States military in any capacity or category.

verdicts.note: In conventional terms Iran is vastly outmatched, though it can impose costs asymmetrically through missiles, drones and shipping attacks.
